events.summary: ADB approved a $200 million facility for economic pressures and trade, investment, and industry reforms.
Initial work began to install a fuel pipeline from Trincomalee Port to the oil tanks.
July Aswesuma elderly allowances for both beneficiary phases were scheduled for bank credit on July 31.
Government plans to preserve the historic hospital and develop it as a museum and tourism attraction.
Government scheduled appointments for 1,444 health-service personnel on August 1.
104 government-purchased Metro buses arrived in Sri Lanka for future public transport service.
Contracts to dispose of SLTB scrap metal were awarded to six companies for Rs. 195,890,193.28.
Cabinet approved long-term leases of five presidential mansions for tourism investment projects.
Cabinet approved establishing a treasury-owned public company to manage multimodal transport centres.
Cabinet approved a committee to prepare a WIPO project proposal protecting Kandy Esala Perahera intellectual property.
Cabinet approved appointing a committee to recommend next steps for developing 60 provincial and local roads.
Cabinet approved replacing 600 standard buses with air-conditioned deluxe buses for long-distance SLTB services.
Authorities arranged drinking water, food and sanitation for pilgrims travelling through Yala.
The minister said the stalled five-storey emergency complex would resume construction at a cost exceeding Rs 1.3 billion.
The minister said Rs 75 million would be allocated soon for hospital development.
Small and medium rice millers received Rs 13.596 billion in deposit loans to buy farmers’ paddy in 2025.
The government provided Rs 132 million in interest subsidies for participating rice millers.
The railway department reopened Andadola and Akurala stations with relief stationmasters after prolonged closures.
Preschool reforms and teacher training are planned to begin in 2027.
Rail services resumed at Anavilundawa with a relief stationmaster assigned.
Railway Department planned special trains for the National Pichchamal Puja on July 25 and 26.
Environmental Authority launched a five-year programme for a plastic-free Kataragama sacred zone.
Gatambe Junction flyover development costs Rs. 14 billion; work restarted in February 2025.
Gatambe Junction flyover development resumed in February 2025 and is under construction.
Rs. 675 million was allocated for widening and developing William Gopallawa Road.
The Mahaiyawa underpass development project is estimated to cost Rs. 650 million.
Rs. 539 million was allocated to develop Louis Pieris Road with dual lanes and sidewalks.
Railway Department temporarily closed Anavilundawa Sub-Railway Station after its station master resigned.
July Aswesuma benefits for 1,224,459 families were credited to beneficiary bank accounts.
Cabinet approved implementation of the updated National Livestock Policy.
Cabinet approved an ADB loan agreement for rooftop solar and virtual net metering.
Cabinet approved a Japanese fund grant agreement for rooftop solar and virtual net metering.
A contract was awarded to expand the Bandaranaike Airport departure terminal.
Cabinet approved awarding Maga Engineering the contract to complete remaining Warakapola bypass construction.
India signed an agreement to provide medical equipment for the new Deniyaya hospital.
The planned 300-bed Deniyaya hospital is estimated to require Rs. 6 billion investment.
Teacher training for the new preschool curriculum is underway.
Government began purchasing Yala-season paddy at 143 warehouses nationwide.
The Meerigama kidney-stone treatment centre opened to the public.
Fertiliser subsidy paid to 667,460 Yala-season farmers.
Government covered added costs to provide urea at a fixed price.
Yala fertiliser subsidy increased to Rs. 30,000 per hectare.
Government paid crop compensation and assistance to 112,442 farmers after Cyclone Ditwah.
Funds allocated to restore tanks, anicuts and canals needed for cultivation.
Paddy Marketing Board plans to begin Yala-season paddy purchases on July 13.
Government provided Rs. 6 billion to the Paddy Marketing Board for paddy purchases.
Rs. 10 billion set aside under deposit loans for millers to stock paddy.
Government plans separate district reserves for urgent bridge, road and building repairs.
Orders issued to establish temporary prisons at Mahamodara and old Bogambara.
University of Colombo decided to hold lectures online for one week amid dengue cases.
Government paid Rs. 12.3415 billion in crop compensation to 202,025 Ditwah-affected farmers.
Economic and psychosocial support programmes had started for 16,000 Aswesuma families.
Government planned to connect 200,000 Aswesuma beneficiary families to productive economic activity.
Officials were directed to plan 50 daycare centres nationwide over the coming years.
Accessibility improvement projects were underway at police stations, hospitals and divisional secretariats.
The old Mahamodara Maternity Hospital buildings were designated as a prison by gazette.
Cabinet agreed to launch a bus clustering pilot on routes 170, 177 and 190.
National programme began conserving archaeological sites, starting work at 100 locations.
Construction of the 50 MW Mannar wind power plant is progressing.
Hayleys Fentons was selected to install and maintain the wind turbines.
Government agencies launched the Badu Shakthi National Tax Week.
Government spending on agriculture totalled Rs. 142 billion in 2025.
Sri Lanka spent US$90.3 million on rice imports from January through May 2026.
The Paddy Marketing Board spent Rs. 19.633 billion purchasing paddy from farmers in 2025.
The Paddy Marketing Board spent Rs. 6.2 billion maintaining a rice buffer stock in 2025.
Government spent Rs. 37 billion on the fertiliser subsidy programme in 2025.
BISTEC GLOBAL donated a digital system for managing dental surgeons’ annual transfers.
Government decided to provide 50 rice dryers to cooperative societies nationwide.
Government set aside decentralized funds to support active and stable cooperative societies.
A presidentially assigned ambulance was transferred to Mullaitivu District General Hospital.
Card payment service launched across 13 Colombo District divisional secretariats.
June Aswesuma elderly allowances scheduled for transfer in two payment phases.
India pledged a reconstruction loan following Cyclone Ditwah.
India pledged grant assistance for Cyclone Ditwah recovery.
Cabinet approved signing agreements to receive India's recovery package.
Cabinet approved the first expressway section using government funds and domestic contractors.
Cabinet approved starting procurement for 535 utility vehicles for government institutions.
Cabinet approved transferring Horana District General Hospital and its assets to the Health Ministry.
Cabinet approved Rs. 6 billion for the 2026 Yala paddy purchase programme.
ADB approved a $200 million emergency loan package for Ditwah recovery and reconstruction.
ADB approved a $500,000 technical assistance grant for Ditwah reconstruction projects.
National Hospital Colombo cath lab complex was scheduled to enter patient services the next day.
Health Ministry established a dengue operations room and public hotline.
